claim: Computed, heuristic and negative: tabu search with exact all-arc cost deltas found no tournament with S_4 on 52, 60, 63 or 66 vertices, using about 87 core-minutes in total. The search minimises the number of undominated 4-sets plus lam * (sum of 5 - |D(T)| over triples T with fewer than 5 dominators). Best (undominated 4-sets, min pair dominators, min triple dominators) per order: N=52 (2141, 11, 4), from QR_47 plus 5 random vertices with lam=0.25; the generic seeds (in-degrees 25/26, QR_67 minus 15 vertices, near-doubly-regular circulants on Z_53 minus a vertex) all stall at 3478-3649. N=60 (2423, 11, 2). N=63 (1393, 13, 3). N=66 (330, 15, 5), which is QR_67 minus one vertex itself. Two exact structural facts were found along the way. First, in QR_67 every single arc reversal creates exactly 40 undominated 4-sets. Second, in QR_67 minus a vertex (330 undominated 4-sets, all triples with >= 5 dominators) the best single reversal still adds a net 29 to the cost, so it is a strict local minimum; 36,640 tabu iterations from it found nothing better. The bounds 52 <= f(4) <= 67 are unchanged. Erdős 902 is not solved.
definitions: A tournament on V: A[w,x]=1 iff w -> x. D(X) = {w not in X : w -> x for all x in X}. S_4: D(X) is nonempty for every 4-set X. U4 = number of 4-sets with D(X) empty. Triple deficit = sum over triples T of max(0, 5 - |D(T)|). Cost(lam) = U4 + lam * triple deficit. Since S_4 forces |D(T)| >= 5 (fact F1), cost 0 holds iff the tournament has S_4. Profile = (U4, min |D(P)| over pairs, min |D(T)| over triples, in-degree histogram). Paley QR_p (p = 3 mod 4 prime): i -> j iff j - i is a nonzero quadratic residue mod p. Seeds: 'reg' = rotational tournament on N vertices randomised by about 10 N^2 score-preserving 3-cycle reversals (in-degrees 25/26 at N=52); 'qr' = QR_67 minus 67-N vertices, the deleted set chosen by swap local search to make the remaining in-degrees as equal as possible (25/26 at N=52), best of 6 by cost; 'circ' = circulant on Z_n (n=N if N is odd, else n=N+1 minus vertex 0), with connection set S chosen by flip local search to minimise the variance of |S cap (S+x)| (doubly-regular-like), excluding QR when n=67; 'qr47' = QR_47 on vertices 0..46 plus N-47 new vertices with fair-coin arcs.
argument:
1. Exact delta formula (proved, short). Reversing an arc u -> v changes |D(X)| only for X that contain exactly one of u and v. For X containing v but not u, |D(X)| drops by 1 iff u dominated X. For X containing u but not v, it rises by 1 iff v -> X \ {u}. So the cost change of every arc at once is a sum over critical objects only. A 4-set with a unique dominator w gives +1 to arcs (w, x) for x in X. An undominated 4-set gives -1 to arcs (x, v) for x in X and v in D(X \ {x}) \ {x}. A triple with |D(T)| <= 5 gives +lam to arcs (w, x) for w in D(T), x in T. A triple with |D(T)| <= 4 gives -lam to arcs (x, v) for v in D(T \ {x}) \ (N^-(x) cup {x}). r8g_core.Tabu.deltas implements this with numpy bitsets and bincount. r8g_validate.py checks it against brute-force recomputation (40 random arcs each at N=20 lam=1, N=24 lam=0.5, and N=66 on QR_67 minus a vertex; error 0), and checks the incremental update against a full recompute.
2. Search: best-move tabu over all arcs (tenure uniform in [8,25], aspiration on a new best, a kick of 4-12 random reversals from the best state after a stall of 1500 iterations, 800 at N=66), restarts of 255-265 s cycling over the seed families. Runs: N=52 lam=1 (6 restarts), N=52 lam=0.25 (3 restarts), N=52 QR_47+5 at lam=1 and lam=0.25 (1 restart each, 130 s), N=60, N=63 and N=66 (3 restarts each, lam=1).
3. Results (exact counts, both checkers agree on the saved best tournaments): see evidence.per_N. No restart reached cost 0, so no S_4 candidate exists and no second-checker verification of a candidate was needed.
4. Structure of QR_67 (exact computation, r8g_structure.json): QR_67 has 22110 4-sets with exactly one dominator. Its automorphism group x -> ax+b (a a nonzero square) is arc-transitive, so each of the 67*33 = 2211 arcs is the unique-dominator arc of 22110*4/2211 = 40 four-sets; the delta matrix confirms min = max = 40. Deleting a vertex uncovers the 22110/67 = 330 four-sets it uniquely dominated. In QR_67 - v the minimum single-reversal delta is +29 (attained by 33 arcs, mean +45.6). So 330 is a strict local minimum, and tabu over 36,640 iterations (two restarts) never went below it. At N=63 and N=60, QR_67 minus 4 or 7 balanced vertices (U4 = 1358 and 2386) was also never beaten in U4. Tabu lowered the weighted cost only by trading undominated 4-sets for triple deficit (U4 1393 and 2423 at the best weighted cost).
5. Interpretation (heuristic, not proof): the generic N=52 seeds all converge to about 3500 undominated 4-sets, while QR_47 + 5 random vertices reaches 2141 within 2 minutes. QR_47 alone has 2162 undominated 4-sets on 47 vertices. So with this budget the search quality is set by seed structure, not by search time, and the landscape near Paley-type tournaments is very rigid: each arc is critical for about 40 four-sets in QR_67. The failure to find S_4 below 67 is therefore weak evidence only.

60.source: QR_67 minus 7 seed (seed U4 2386, seed cost 3306)

63.source: QR_67 minus 4 seed (seed U4 1358, seed cost 1635)

66.source: QR_67 minus one vertex, never improved (18672 + 17968 tabu iterations)

evidence.compute: numpy bitsets only. gcc/clang/MSVC are not installed; numba was tried in an isolated folder but its DLLs are blocked by the Windows Application Control policy, so it was removed. Speed is about 6-27 ms per full-neighbourhood iteration. Search time: main runs 26.7 + 26.2 + 26.8 core-min, QR_47 runs 2 x 2.25, tuning about 3, total about 87 core-minutes on at most 3 cores.
evidence.logs: research/compute/r8g_log_{N}_{tag}.json (per restart: seed, trace, profile), research/compute/r8g_out_p1..p3.txt, research/compute/r8g_summary.json

weaknesses: Heuristic search with a small budget (about 87 core-minutes, numpy-only throughput of about 40-170 iterations per second, roughly 9000 iterations per 265 s restart). A failure to find S_4 is weak evidence and says nothing rigorous about f(4). The search is clearly far from the global optimum at N=52: generic seeds plateau near 3500 undominated 4-sets, while the QR_47+5 seed reaches 2141 in 2 minutes, after only one restart per lam. The objective weight lam changes which local optima are reached; only lam = 1 and 0.25 were tried. Only single-arc reversals were used: no score-preserving 3-cycle moves, no vertex-row replacement moves, and no k-flip neighbourhoods. At N=66 every QR-type restart is the same tournament up to isomorphism, so its restarts differ only in the tabu RNG. The tight-pair structure from the lower-bound analysis (|D(P)| = 11, 5-regular R, J >= 6) was not imposed. The saved N=60 and N=63 files are the best weighted-cost states; the plain QR_67-deletion seeds have slightly lower U4 (2386 and 1358).
references: R. L. Graham and J. H. Spencer, A constructive solution to a tournament problem, Canad. Math. Bull. 14 (1971) 45-48 (Paley tournaments have S_k)
E. Szekeres and G. Szekeres, On a problem of Schütte and Erdős, Math. Gaz. 49 (1965) 290-293
next_step: Turn the strongest structured seed into an exact finite question: does QR_47 (or QR_43) extend to an S_4 tournament on 52 vertices by adding 5 (or 9) new vertices? With the QR core fixed this is a CP-SAT/SAT model with 5*47 + 10 = 245 Boolean arcs and one clause per 4-set (each clause lists the possible new dominators, plus the fixed old ones), which is small enough to decide outright. At N=66, add vertex-row replacement and 2-flip moves to escape the QR_67 - v basin (single reversals cost at least +29 there), or decide exactly by SAT whether any tournament within Hamming distance k of QR_67 - v has S_4, for small k.
relation_to_prior: R4-D excluded named algebraic families and all induced subtournaments of QR_67, QR_71, QR_79, QR_83 on 52-66 vertices. This task searches general tournaments by arc reversal from three new seed families (25/26 near-regular, balanced QR_67 deletions, near-doubly-regular circulants) and QR_47+5, at N = 52, 60, 63, 66. It does not reuse any exhausted approach key. random-cayley-beat-erdos-upper concerned random Cayley tournaments for the asymptotic bound; here circulants serve only as local-search seeds.
novelty: (i) An exact all-arcs cost-change formula and a validated vectorised tabu engine for S_4. (ii) Exact facts: in QR_67 every arc reversal creates exactly 40 undominated 4-sets (arc-transitivity plus 22110 unique-dominator 4-sets), and QR_67 minus a vertex is a strict local minimum of the cost with minimum single-reversal delta +29. (iii) Empirical: at N=52 the reachable optimum depends strongly on the seed (about 3500 from generic seeds vs 2141 from QR_47+5), which points to Paley-extension models as the next exact test. No counterexample to f(4) >= 53 was found, and f(4) <= 67 is not improved.
